muse-code.userNote: A yielded bash command reports background_running through its result with no registry item; the workflow row is the background process the sidebar draws.
muse-code.detailNote: A yielded bash command reports background_running through its result with no registry item; the workflow row is the background process the sidebar draws.

reasonix.detailNote:
Re-evaluated on 2026-10-29 against the installed Reasonix v2.53.1 binary and matching source tag, revision 74805c102cf483aed637f30c9316928d3048c18c. Source: internal/frontend/acp/dispatch.go and internal/runtime/delegation/task.go. The native read-only task supplies its prompt and final report. Acceptance verifies the child tab, Markdown, exact Copy, and quoted failure text that does not change the actual outcome.

Browser acceptance: all 2 case(s) in the complete spec passed with zero retries in e2e-sjioUn. The complete Reasonix run passed 84 cases in all 54 files.

amp.userNote: Amp's stream shows a subagent only as a call and a final report. It sends no messages and no session for the subagent, so LeapMux has no subagent tab for Amp.
amp.detailNote:
The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity.

Classified as an agent limit: the stream-JSON adapter of Amp 0.0.1791074829 ignores each message that has a `parentToolUseId`, so only the parent `tool_use` and the final `tool_result` of `Task`, `oracle`, `librarian`, and `finder` reach stdout (installed bundle, checked 2026-10-05). The internal thread-actor protocol does carry child messages, but it is undocumented and LeapMux does not speak it; medium confidence because of that alternative.

dirac.userNote: Each Dirac subagent opens its own tab. The tab shows the prompt and loads the full history when the subagent ends. Dirac does not stream the full transcript while the subagent runs.
dirac.detailNote: Dirac and Fast Agent open a child tab for each subagent. The tab shows its prompt and loads the native message history when the child ends. Neither agent streams its full child transcript while it runs. Fast Agent's [Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tracker](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L236-L260) creates a tool ID that differs from the model ID in its [child snapshot](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/agents/subagent_tool.py#L829-L833). Its [ACP completion](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L873-L900) sends result text without a child ID. When equal results cannot identify one archive, LeapMux closes the ambiguous child with an archive-unavailable report.

fast-agent.userNote: Each Fast Agent subagent opens its own tab. The tab shows the prompt and loads the full history when the subagent ends. If Fast Agent gives no unique ID for a result, LeapMux closes that tab with an archive-unavailable report.
fast-agent.detailNote: Dirac and Fast Agent open a child tab for each subagent. The tab shows its prompt and loads the native message history when the child ends. Neither agent streams its full child transcript while it runs. Fast Agent's [Agent Client Protocol (ACP) tracker](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L236-L260) creates a tool ID that differs from the model ID in its [child snapshot](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/agents/subagent_tool.py#L829-L833). Its [ACP completion](https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/blob/07c460ee395843b91e2bf71a5136f0b6b2886852/src/fast_agent/acp/tool_progress.py#L873-L900) sends result text without a child ID. When equal results cannot identify one archive, LeapMux closes the ambiguous child with an archive-unavailable report.

deepseek-harness.userNote: The child tab shows the messages of the child agent and each later message that the parent agent sends to it. It hides the instruction and context messages that DeepSeek Harness injects.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-child-controls-probe: a real continuable child has its own live follow stream. Its completed first turn starts an exact parent report. Native subagents/prompt sends the next prompt to the same child; that request retains the old child answer. interruptByParent closes the second turn as aborted with cause user. The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84. The child tab shows the native prompt (source user, no rpcId). A later message of the parent agent from send_message is a user message with source agent-message in @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 (createAgentMessage, submitAdmitted). LeapMux stores it nowhere else for the child tab, so the tab keeps it. A Go unit test covers this input kind; no browser spec sends it. Injected instruction-file and runtime-context messages are not shown. A child message to the root session and the team-message kind of the experimental team profile are not stored; no probe has checked them.

gemini-cli.userNote: Each Gemini CLI subagent opens its own tab. Gemini CLI links a subagent to its root session and not to its direct parent.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Child UUID and owning root session are exact native storage identities. Gemini stores nested descendants under the root and omits direct-parent links.

command-code.userNote: The child tab holds the prompt that Command Code gave the child and its final report. Command Code sends no full child transcript.
command-code.detailNote: The native agent opener supplies the exact child prompt. The native tool result supplies the final report. LeapMux stores these in the child tab. The supported native API supplies no complete child text or tool-result transcript.

muse-code.detailNote: Muse 1.4.13-R6996.1 supplies childSessionId and subagentId on native workflow child items. Native mock run-ZqV08v reads completed child history through session/read and view/page; run-kvgUgw also reads its 51-record stored log through log/streams and log/page after a fresh live subscription refuses the unloaded child. LeapMux links the actual native session, replays ordered stored/live history, preserves raw tool evidence and keeps worker-owned user rows single. Browser e2e-LTZCK8 proves the actual child tab, native progress/tool output, owned session and spans, and reload. Fresh-process native resume probe resume-ZGvySh restores the actual child metadata and delivers its followup in one mock request with zero unexpected. The worker-restart browser case retains the same native child and message identities, delivers a new child note, and preserves one user/answer row after reload. Parent history is not replayed. Native acceptance: Native CLI mock probes recorded under .tmp/muse-current-probe/. Final Muse race package: 1002 passed in .tmp/final-focused-repairs-2.log. Complete Muse directory: 84 passed, zero retries/skips/flaky/unexpected, all 54 files match discovery in e2e-LTZCK8 (.tmp/broad-validation-audio-04.log); the combined three-provider report has 255 first-attempt passes. Native actor/session identities, original bytes and worker-owned user rows remain verified.

cursor.userNote: Cursor streams the messages of a subagent while it runs, and LeapMux shows them in the subagent tab.
cursor.detailNote: The native Cursor subagent capability streams child messages before completion. LeapMux routes those messages to the child transcript. See providers/cursor/subagent.go.

kilo.userNote: The subagent tab shows the subagent's own messages and tool calls while it runs, before its final report.
kilo.detailNote:
Kilo runs each subagent as a child session, and its ACP adapter streams a session only to a client that loaded it. The parent's running task call states the child session on the daemon's event stream before the child's first request, so LeapMux then loads that session with session/load and routes its updates to the subagent's transcript. The load replays what the session already holds, so output from before the load is not lost. A child's permission request now reaches the reader too, as a request of a session that LeapMux serves.

Verified with Kilo 7.8.16. All 150 OpenCode and Kilo browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-FQDjcm. All 1,140 ACP, OpenCode and Kilo backend race tests passed.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/516.

opencode.userNote: The subagent tab shows the subagent's own messages and tool calls while it runs, before its final report.
opencode.detailNote:
OpenCode runs each subagent as a child session, and its ACP adapter streams a session only to a client that loaded it. The parent's running task call states the child session on the daemon's event stream before the child's first request, so LeapMux then loads that session with session/load and routes its updates to the subagent's transcript. The load replays what the session already holds, so output from before the load is not lost. A child's permission request now reaches the reader too, as a request of a session that LeapMux serves.

Verified with OpenCode 1.19.4. All 150 OpenCode and Kilo browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-FQDjcm. All 1,140 ACP, OpenCode and Kilo backend race tests passed.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/516.

goose.userNote: LeapMux shows the tool calls of a Goose subagent while it runs. Goose sends no text from the subagent.
goose.detailNote: A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

pi.userNote: The `pi-subagents` extension sends LeapMux progress counts and a final report for a subagent. The messages of a running subagent stay inside Pi. The child tab shows the prompt when the subagent starts and the report when it ends.
pi.detailNote:
Kilo, OpenCode, Pi and Reasonix deliver the subagent's transcript when it completes: the prompt at spawn and the report at the end. A background spawn of Kilo, OpenCode or Reasonix keeps the prompt only.

Classified as an agent limit: the foreground update of the Agent tool in pi-subagents carries tool use count, token count, status and an activity line, and no messages. The extension writes the transcript of each subagent to its own output file, and LeapMux reads no output file. The conversation viewer is a terminal-only overlay.

Tested version: Pi 1.0.0.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix supplies a subagent's report when the subagent ends. The subagent tab shows its prompt while it runs.
reasonix.detailNote:
Re-evaluated on 2026-10-29 against the installed Reasonix v2.53.1 binary and matching source tag, revision 74805c102cf483aed637f30c9316928d3048c18c. Source: internal/frontend/acp/dispatch.go. ACP supplies no child-session route for live text or tool updates. The child tab retains its prompt while the child runs and receives only its final report. Actual child tool execution verifies this limit.

Browser acceptance: all 1 case(s) in the complete spec passed with zero retries in e2e-sjioUn. The complete Reasonix run passed 84 cases in all 54 files.

zcode.userNote: LeapMux shows the tool calls of a ZCode subagent while it runs. The subagent's text arrives as the final report.
zcode.detailNote: A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

codewhale.userNote: LeapMux shows each message of a CodeWhale subagent when that message ends, with about half a second of lag.
codewhale.detailNote: A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

qwen-code.userNote: LeapMux shows a long text run of a subagent when its message ends, not word by word. Rows of a background subagent lag by about half a second.
qwen-code.detailNote:
A transcript streams at message boundaries: a long text run appears when its message or turn ends. Goose streams the child's tool rows only, and its text never arrives. ZCode streams the tool cards live and sends the child's text as the final report. Codewhale and Qwen Code tail a transcript file, with about half a second of lag.

Qwen Code streams a foreground subagent in the parent session as session updates. LeapMux tails a transcript file only for a background subagent. The statement above that Qwen Code tails a transcript file therefore holds for background subagents only (checked 2026-10-05).

amp.userNote: Amp's stream drops the messages of a running subagent. LeapMux shows nothing from the subagent until its final report arrives in the result of the call.
amp.detailNote:
The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity.

Classified as an agent limit: Amp 0.0.1791074829 stream-JSON prints no child message while a subagent runs (installed bundle, checked 2026-10-05). The E2E spec shows the child model request while the parent transcript holds none of the child progress. The thread-actor protocol streams child deltas, but LeapMux does not speak it; medium confidence because of that alternative.

cline.userNote: LeapMux shows one running Cline subagent live. When two subagents run at the same time, their transcripts appear only when they finish.
cline.detailNote: Cline streams one subagent live. When two run at the same time, their transcripts appear when they finish.

dirac.userNote: While a Dirac subagent runs, its tab shows the prompt and short progress lines. Dirac gives the full tool transcript only after the subagent ends.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac exposes the child prompt while the child runs, then restores its full tool transcript at the completed native archive boundary. A held native child Read produces no live tool row before that boundary.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. The Dirac 0.5.17 subagent card sends a trajectory of at most 80 events. Each text is cut to a fixed length. The card has no structured child tool rows (source checked 2026-10-05). LeapMux already shows the message and tool digest lines live. LeapMux restores the full tool transcript from the archive after the child ends. LeapMux drops the tool_result digest events, so a LeapMux limit is the alternative classification.

fast-agent.userNote: While a Fast Agent subagent runs, its tab shows the prompt. Fast Agent gives the full tool transcript only after the subagent ends.
fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent exposes the child prompt while the child runs, then restores its full tool transcript at the completed native archive boundary. A held native child Read produces no live tool row before that boundary.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. Fast Agent 0.10.42 runs the child with one generate call and no tool execution handler. It writes the child session to disk (source checked 2026-10-05). The E2E run shows no live tool row before LeapMux reads the archive.

deepseek-harness.userNote: The child tab updates while the child works, including its tool activity, before its final report arrives.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: web-child-controls-probe: a real continuable child has its own live follow stream. Its completed first turn starts an exact parent report. Native subagents/prompt sends the next prompt to the same child; that request retains the old child answer. interruptByParent closes the second turn as aborted with cause user. The parent consumes the native stopped report. Six strict mock requests, two exact parent reports, zero unexpected requests. Native version 0.2.0-rc.2, source commit 639ed015397290b3745d163aafe02ffee4aa3f84.

gemini-cli.userNote: The tab of a Gemini CLI subagent fills while the subagent runs. Gemini CLI sends no live stream for a subagent, so LeapMux shows each completed model or tool step after Gemini CLI saves it.
gemini-cli.detailNote: Native JSONL records reach the child tab before final report completion. Native files supply completed model/tool records; ACP provides no child stream.

command-code.userNote: While a child runs, its tab shows short activity notices from Command Code. It shows no child text and no full tool result.
command-code.detailNote: The native subagent_progress event supplies abbreviated tool activity and token estimates. It drops child text and full tool results. The child tab shows each activity notice while the child runs, before its final report. It shows no child text and no full tool result.

muse-code.detailNote: Muse 1.4.13-R6996.1 native mock run-LvwUdF holds a real child after shell stdout: view/subscribe succeeds, the stored view has progress before completion, and nine later child notifications include another command and the turn end (five model requests, zero unexpected). LeapMux buffers live overlap while replaying history. Native e2e-NK5cgb exposes an early empty stored page despite live head3; the regression-first adapter keeps the initial prefix pending and coalesces a new read on real child events. Browser e2e-LTZCK8 proves output before release, later output and finality in the actual child tab. Native e2e-ydVvIk also proves a partial stored page containing only branch cursor1 after live head3. LeapMux waits for the exact observed head in the stored prefix, retains initial history across view gaps, and never treats buffered live overlap as proof of earlier history. Native acceptance: Native CLI mock probes recorded under .tmp/muse-current-probe/. Final Muse race package: 1002 passed in .tmp/final-focused-repairs-2.log. Complete Muse directory: 84 passed, zero retries/skips/flaky/unexpected, all 54 files match discovery in e2e-LTZCK8 (.tmp/broad-validation-audio-04.log); the combined three-provider report has 255 first-attempt passes. Native actor/session identities, original bytes and worker-owned user rows remain verified.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code lets a user message a subagent in its own terminal app. The input stream that LeapMux uses cannot address one subagent, so the child tab is read-only.
claude-code.detailNote:
Claude Code's TUI can send a message to a Task subagent. It queues the message while the child runs or resumes an idle child. LeapMux drives Claude over stream-json stdin. Its user message carries no child or task ID, so typed input reaches the root session. The child tab is read-only. A direct subagent wire path is required to change this.

Classified as an agent limit: in the Claude Code 2.1.289 bundle the user message schema has no field that identifies a subagent, and the control requests include stop_task but no request that sends a message to a task. The Remote Control bridge in the bundle ignores an inbound user frame that has a parent_tool_use_id, as an echo of a subagent frame. The headless documentation (checked 2026-10-05) uses parent_tool_use_id only to mark subagent output. The terminal app reaches a subagent through its own in-process path.

codex.userNote: Codex rejects direct input to a subagent that Multi-Agent V2 starts, so the child tab is read-only. Upstream tracks this in [openai/codex#33885](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33885).
codex.detailNote:
Codex Multi-Agent V2 rejects direct app-server input for spawned child threads. LeapMux keeps their transcripts read-only. See providers/codex/provider.go.

Classified as an agent limit: Codex Multi-Agent V2 child threads are read-only. Both turn/start and turn/steer answer "direct app-server input is not allowed for multi-agent v2 sub-agents". Upstream issues 33885 and 34377 ask for direct input and are open (checked 2026-10-05).

Tested version: Codex 0.160.0.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/33885> (open): Reports that MultiAgentV2 child threads are read-only and that app-server clients get "direct app-server input is not allowed for multi-agent v2 sub-agents".

cursor.userNote: Cursor announces each subagent with no input capability and takes no message for it. The subagent tab stays read-only while the subagent runs.
cursor.detailNote:
Cursor provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 sends subagent_spawned with capabilities {} and accepts session/prompt for the parent session only (installed bundle read 2026-10-05).

github-copilot.userNote: A message typed in the tab of a background subagent reaches that subagent. A running subagent reads it in its next turn, and an idle one starts a turn for it. A foreground subagent takes no message, because Copilot never passes it one.
github-copilot.detailNote:
LeapMux sends the message with Copilot's task message (session.tasks.sendMessage) to the agent task that the subagent's spawning tool call started (session.tasks.list). Copilot keeps a background subagent after each turn, idle, so its row stays paused and its tab stays open; a message to a running one waits for the turn that follows. A foreground subagent accepts the message but never reads it, so its tab is read-only.

Verified with Copilot CLI 1.0.87. All 81 Copilot browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-Avsj8A, including a background subagent that read a message sent while it ran and one sent while it waited, with its row paused between its turns. All 634 tests of the Copilot package and the shared agent test package passed, also under the race detector.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/505.

kilo.userNote: A message typed in the tab of a running subagent reaches that subagent, which reads it during its run. A subagent that finished takes no message.
kilo.detailNote:
LeapMux sends the message as a second prompt on the subagent's own session, which it loaded for the live transcript, as the parent's own steer works; the prompt carries the subagent's own agent and model. Kilo holds a prompt that arrives during a turn until that turn ends, and the parent's task waits until the child read it. A subagent whose task call ended takes no message, because a turn that it started would reach no one: the parent already read the subagent's result.

Verified with Kilo 7.8.16. All 150 OpenCode and Kilo browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-FQDjcm. All 1,140 ACP, OpenCode and Kilo backend race tests passed.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/517.

opencode.userNote: A message typed in the tab of a running subagent reaches that subagent, which reads it during its run. A subagent that finished takes no message.
opencode.detailNote:
LeapMux sends the message as a second prompt on the subagent's own session, which it loaded for the live transcript, as the parent's own steer works; the prompt carries the subagent's own agent and model. OpenCode adds the message to the running turn, so the child's next request holds it. A subagent whose task call ended takes no message, because a turn that it started would reach no one: the parent already read the subagent's result.

Verified with OpenCode 1.19.4. All 150 OpenCode and Kilo browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-FQDjcm. All 1,140 ACP, OpenCode and Kilo backend race tests passed.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/517.

goose.userNote: Goose runs a subagent inside a tool call and has no way to send it a message while it runs. The subagent tab stays read-only.
goose.detailNote:
Goose provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: Goose 1.53.0 runs a subagent as a delegate tool task with no session of its own on ACP, and the summon extension offers only the load and delegate tools (source read 2026-10-05).

pi.userNote: The `pi-subagents` extension routes a message to a running subagent only in the Pi terminal app. In other modes the text goes to the main model, so the child tab is read-only.
pi.detailNote:
Pi provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: the input handler of pi-subagents sets canDispatchDirectly only when ctx.mode is tui, and its comment states that steering and resuming are not available in headless modes. The steer_subagent tool is a model tool, not a client request.

Tested version: Pi 1.0.0.

reasonix.userNote: Reasonix exposes no way to send a message to a running subagent. Its tab stays read-only.
reasonix.detailNote:
Re-evaluated on 2026-10-29 against the installed Reasonix v2.53.1 binary and matching source tag, revision 74805c102cf483aed637f30c9316928d3048c18c. Source: internal/frontend/acp/service.go. No ACP or vendor method addresses a running task as a child conversation. A live native child therefore keeps a read-only tab; root session inbox methods do not address that child.

Browser acceptance: all 1 case(s) in the complete spec passed with zero retries in e2e-sjioUn. The complete Reasonix run passed 84 cases in all 54 files.

zcode.userNote: ZCode 3.14.4 refuses input to a subagent session, because it treats that session as read-only. [An open upstream request](https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/659) asks for messages to active subagents.
zcode.detailNote:
ZCode provides no child-directed composer input route in LeapMux. Its child tab remains read-only while the native task runs.

Classified as an agent limit: both session/send and the v4 command admission in ZCode 3.14.4 throw 'Subagent sessions are read-only' (reasonCode guard.subagentReadOnly) for a session of type subagent_child (zcode.cjs, checked 2026-10-05). Upstream issue zai-org/feedback#659 (open) asks for dynamic sub-agent steering.

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/zai-org/feedback/issues/659> (open): A feature request for mid-task message queuing and real-time messages from the main agent to active sub-agents.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale's runtime has no route that sends a message to a running subagent. Only the model can message a subagent, so the subagent tab is read-only.
codewhale.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: in CodeWhale 0.10.0 the actions `message` and `followup` belong to the model-facing `agent` tool, and the HTTP API serves only `GET /v1/agent-runs` and `GET /v1/agent-runs/{id}` for runs (research and source checked 2026-10-05).

kimi-code.userNote: Kimi Code accepts a message that you type in the subagent tab while the subagent runs.
kimi-code.detailNote: Kimi Code accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code accepts a message typed in the subagent tab while the subagent runs.
mimo-code.detailNote: MiMo Code accepts a typed message from its subagent tab while the child runs.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code gives a client no way to send a message to a subagent. Only the parent model can do it, so the subagent tab stays read-only.
qwen-code.detailNote:
The child transcript exists, but the current provider bridge exposes no direct input route for that child. Its composer is read-only.

Classified as an agent limit: the extension methods of Qwen Code 0.24.7 for a client (qwen/control/session/*) list task cancel and workflow actions. They list no message route to a child. The send_message tool is for the model (checked 2026-10-05).

oh-my-pi.detailNote: Verified with installed Oh My Pi 18.12.6 and source commit 0b5c27ab24719c86a5986b95ee55f4e75bc1aaa0 on 2026-10-22. The native steer_subagent command delivers text to the selected running child. LeapMux resolves the complete session-scoped child key and preserves native errors. Child text attachments are inlined; the native command has no image field. The complete browser spec proved the child model request received the steered message, the child transcript retained it, and the parent accepted another prompt. Both complete child-control browser specs passed with zero retries in e2e-Gv41gl.

grok-build.userNote: Send text with Steer while the subagent runs. Subagent attachments are not supported.
grok-build.detailNote:
Verified with Grok Build 1.0.70 through the isolated E2E mock only. LeapMux pins the user-approved GROK_ACTIVE_AGENT_MESSAGES=1 feature before initialization. The native subagent_spawned update supplies an opaque agentAddress, distinct from the child session UUID. The adapter retains that owned address and sends one literal text block to _x.ai/subagent/message with the current parent session and queue=false. A native accepted reply needs a nonempty messageId. Refusals preserve the queued input, and uncertain admission remains uncertain instead of authorizing a repeated send. Missing routes, an empty root session and a stopped process send no request. Context clear and child completion remove old address routes. The native engine adds its own cross-agent provenance prefix to model context; LeapMux preserves it.

Native evidence: .tmp/grok-child-probe/drive-2.log, run-CNuTQg, six scripted model requests and zero unexpected requests. The first probe proves that a child UUID is refused. The live successful child request contains the exact message and both segments of a real held command. All 292 Grok Go race tests pass. The complete child-message spec passes with zero retries in e2e-042juE, including one stored child input and answer after reload, no parent transcript contamination and a completed native child row. Native acceptance: all 77 cases in the complete Grok Build directory passed with zero retries in e2e-GvGlff, including the separate audio refusal spec. All 292 Grok Go race tests passed. zcode.userNote: You can steer a running ZCode turn. ZCode adds your message to the turn after the running tool finishes, or continues the turn with it after the model's answer. If you interrupt the turn first, the message returns to the queue and runs as the next turn. A message with an image or another binary file goes in the next turn.
zcode.detailNote:
LeapMux sends a steer through ZCode's command inbox (`v4/command`, a `sendText` with the `guide` delivery) on the stdio app-server. ZCode injects it into the running turn at the next boundary: after a tool result, or after the model's answer, where the turn continues. The model reads it as the user's own message. LeapMux writes the steer's row when ZCode reports that it drained the steer (`turn.steerDrained`). Before an interrupt, and after a turn that ends with a steer still queued (a failed turn keeps it there), LeapMux takes the steer back (`deleteQueueItem`), so the queue runs it as the next turn instead of ZCode draining it into the conversation unread. A steer carries text only, because the command inbox takes uploaded attachment references rather than inline data. This route replaces the earlier session-mailbox route, which presented the steer to the model as reference material from another session.

Verified with ZCode 3.16.3 through private native probes of a steer after a tool result, after a streamed answer, before an interrupt with and without the withdrawal, at a failed turn, and while no turn ran. All 90 ZCode browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-yRHQz0, including a steer after a tool result, a steer that continues a streamed answer, and a steer pending at an interrupt that returns to the queue and runs once. qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code reads a steered message after the running tool batch ends. If the turn ends without another tool batch, LeapMux sends the message as the next prompt.
qwen-code.detailNote: Cursor's protocol exposes no steer method. The installed Goose ACP handshake advertises no steer method, so LeapMux offers Preempt. Reasonix steers only when its CLI advertises a steer method. Qwen Code takes a steer at its next tool gap.

amp.userNote: A new Amp conversation offers steering after its first reply supplies a native thread ID.
amp.detailNote: A new conversation has no native thread ID until Amp sends its first reply. LeapMux offers steering after that reply. A resumed conversation already has its thread ID. The native spec checks both states.

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code steers a running turn with text only. If the message attaches an image, a PDF, or another binary file, LeapMux sends the whole message as the next turn.
codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy Code accepts text while it works. Its stream-JSON steering path converts `control_request/steer.content_blocks` to text.

The steer handler of CodeBuddy 2.160.0 keeps the text of the content blocks only. SteerInput therefore refuses a non-text file, and the worker sends the whole input as the next turn. No image filename goes to the model as steer text. The image bytes reach the model in the next turn.

junie.detailNote:
Verified with Junie 3419.7. LeapMux sends _session/steering with sessionId and prompt blocks. The installed SteeringHandler delegates to JunieAgentSession.steer, whose response distinguishes injected from startedNewTurn. The existing adapter tracks a new native turn through lastRequestComplete and keeps injected input inside the active turn. Native bytecode evidence: .tmp/junie-steering-probe/{handler,agent-support,agent-session}.txt. The complete steering spec passed both cases with zero retries in e2e-L3etvh: a steer during a text stream starts its own turn; a steer while a real shell command runs reaches the next request with output written before and after the steer, leaves one result divider, persists once after reload and permits the next ordinary turn. All requests use the isolated E2E mock. Native acceptance: all 79 cases in the complete Junie directory passed with zero retries in e2e-SznWZ5. All 154 Junie Go race tests passed. Frontend type checking and lint passed. The script before-proof failed exactly the new Junie assertion plus the separately pending Codex audio assertion; all other 3430 script tests passed.

fast-agent.detailNote:

Classified as an agent limit. Fast Agent 0.10.42 has no steering term in its source. Its ACP server runs one prompt task for each session (source checked 2026-10-05). The Worker keeps the input queued after its own refusal.

The next model request contains that exact steering text and the actual command output. Two strict mock requests, one durable turn end, zero unexpected requests. gemini-cli.detailNote:

Classified as an agent limit. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 has model steering only in its terminal interface. Its ACP code has no steering term (source checked 2026-10-05). The initialize response has no steer capability. A concurrent session/prompt aborts the pending prompt. The Worker offers Preempt and keeps the input queued.

SteerInput of LeapMux returns ErrSteeringUnsupported for a non-text attachment, so the worker queues the message as the next turn.

The Worker draws one Subagent row per workflow_agent entry under the run's workflow:<name> group (workflow.go); the agent's settled state ends its row, and the run's task_notification ends every unsettled agent row with the run's own outcome. A workflow agent owns no transcript, so its row links no child agent. The installed native addon’s featureFlagsMetadata identifies agent_factories as availability=staff (.tmp/copilot-workflow/feature-metadata.log). Both direct probes use the E2E mock and make zero model requests or unexpected requests. The prior real-account metadata probes also found no factory/workflow tools; they made no model turn. These facts establish a native restriction for the tested non-staff session, not a claim about every possible account. The browser spec still creates two real native children, proves the absent workflow catalog and retains their ordinary ungrouped rows after reload. A factoryRunId in an unreachable staff feature does not establish public workflow availability. Native acceptance: all 85 Copilot browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-qPUb1T (85 passed results, zero skipped/unexpected/flaky), including the workflow catalog/children proof and the separate new audio refusal. zcode.userNote: The Background tasks sidebar shows each subagent task of a ZCode workflow under the workflow's own row, with the subagent's name and the status of its task.
zcode.detailNote:
ZCode 3.16.3 states a `CreateWorkflow` run as one background task. Its subagents (`agent(...)` in the script) and their tasks (`ask`) reach a client only through the conversation subscription of ZCode's desktop protocol (`v4/conversation/subscribe` with workflow-run deltas). Its first frame states each run's actors and nodes, and `workflowRun.updated` states what changed. LeapMux holds the subscription open while a run works, and draws one row for each ask node under the run's row: the subagent's name over the head of its instructions, and the status from the node's phase and outcome. ZCode can end the background task before the frame that settles the last node, so the subscription stays open until the frames report the run's end. A deterministic `world.run` read gets no row.

Verified with ZCode 3.16.3 through a private native probe of a run with two named subagents, also with a subscription that started while the run worked. All 93 ZCode browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-MlkPos, including a run with two named subagents whose rows ended as succeeded under the run's own row. All 1,745 tests of the ZCode package and the shared provider kit passed under the race detector.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/520.

codewhale.userNote: CodeWhale reports a workflow as one item with a status. It sends no row for each child, so LeapMux shows one workflow row and has nothing to group under it.
codewhale.detailNote:
Claude Code runs a Workflow child but sends LeapMux only the top-level workflow task row. Codewhale and Qwen send one self-grouped workflow row but no separate child or stage row. One row does not group work.

Classified as an agent limit: the `workflow` result metadata of CodeWhale 0.10.0 holds the run id, the status, and the terminal flag; the child `agent.*` events never reach a runtime thread, and no field ties a child to the workflow. The E2E spec shows two native units inside one opaque row. Medium confidence: the `/v1/agent-runs` records might link children to a workflow, and LeapMux does not read them for that (research and source checked 2026-10-05).

qwen-code.userNote: The Background tasks sidebar shows each agent of a workflow run as its own row, grouped under the workflow's name with the run itself.
qwen-code.detailNote: Qwen Code 0.26.0 reports a workflow run's agents only through the task list: `qwen/status/session/tasks` with `includeWorkflows: true` states each run (id, toolUseId, label, status, currentPhase) and one entry per dispatch (stable id, label, prompt, status queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled). The Worker polls the list while a workflow row is open (`workflow.go`) and draws one Subagent row per dispatch under the run row's group; a settled dispatch closes its row, the run's final tool-call frame triggers one last read (the list keeps settled runs) and ends every unsettled dispatch row with the run's own outcome. A workflow agent owns no transcript, so its row links no child agent. Native probes: .tmp/qwen-wf-probe/tasks-final.json (two dispatches completed), tasks-t02.json (live list). Native acceptance: all 80 Qwen Code browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-CYzc9h; 173 package tests including the seven new workflow tests.

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi has no workflow feature that groups work. It reports each subagent as a separate task.
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
The native output provides no workflow group that contains at least two work rows.

Classified as an agent limit, with low confidence: Oh My Pi 18.6.0 has no workflow concept in its RPC protocol. Its subagent_lifecycle frames carry index and parentToolCallId, so the subagents that one task call starts share a parent call. That is a grouping that LeapMux could derive, and it is not a native workflow group. The maintainers can decide to treat it as one.

amp.userNote: Amp's stream has no workflow structure. Each subagent call appears as its own row, so LeapMux groups none of them.
amp.detailNote:
The stream also carries no child messages and no workflow activity.

Classified as an agent limit: Amp 0.0.1791074829 shows cross-thread tools (`create_thread`, `wait_for_threads`) and `Task` calls as ordinary tool calls with no group key (research checked 2026-10-05). The E2E spec shows two separate rows with no workflow heading.

junie.userNote: Junie reports each subagent as a separate row with no workflow grouping, so the Background tasks sidebar shows no workflow heading.
junie.detailNote:
Junie reports independent native child rows without workflow grouping metadata. Two real children retain separate completed/running states. Their loaded Worker registry contains no workflow row or group before or after reload.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence: subagent_spawned and subagent_state_update of Junie 26.9.22 carry the child session id, name, task, and state, and no workflow or group field (checked 2026-10-05).

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code reports a workflow only as one background process with phase counts. It sends no separate row for each agent of a workflow, so LeapMux shows no workflow group.
letta-code.detailNote:
Letta Code's `Workflow` tool exists in the toolset but emits no workflow grouping events on the wire. A background process summary can carry `kind:"workflow"`, and LeapMux draws no group from it.

Classified as an agent limit with low confidence: the background process snapshot of Letta Code 0.34.2 holds per-phase counts for a workflow, not one row for each workflow agent (installed letta.js checked 2026-10-05). LeapMux could draw the phase counts as a group, so a LeapMux limit is possible.

dirac.userNote: Dirac reports each subagent on its own and sends no workflow group, so the sidebar lists the subagents as separate rows.
dirac.detailNote:
Dirac reports independent native child rows without workflow grouping metadata. Two real children retain separate completed/running states. Their loaded Worker registry contains no workflow row or group before or after reload.

Classified as an agent limit. The Dirac 0.5.17 child card input holds isSubagent, agentId, agentName, taskTitle and prompt. It has no group or workflow field (source checked 2026-10-05).

Missions (its multi-agent workflows) are a one-shot `exec` surface and are refused on the streaming input LeapMux drives, so no workflow grouping appears.

Classified as an agent limit: Droid 0.233.0 refuses --mission with stream-json and stream-jsonrpc input, and LeapMux drives stream-jsonrpc (installed binary strings checked 2026-10-05).

gemini-cli.detailNote: Native closed-session proof uses installed 0.62.0 and the strict local mock. A session closed and reopened inside the same UTC minute fails native session/load with -32603 (No previous sessions found), because 0.62.0 names its archive for the minute and appends to the original file; upstream fixed that collision in [upstream fix](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/29463) ([native session issue](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28693)), first released in v0.63.0-preview.0; stable 0.62.0 does NOT carry the fix, so the browser spec reopens a session archived in an earlier minute. A session from an earlier minute loads, and the reopened tab restores the stored LeapMux transcript and serves the next model request with the original native context. Gemini also starts native history replay without awaiting completion ([history replay issue](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/28775)), so replayed text can trail the session/load reply; the worker consumes that idle replay for the current session instead of storing it beside the copied transcript, and a prompt never inherits text buffered before it started.

Verified with CodeBuddy Code 2.172.1. LeapMux enables --include-partial-messages and consumes native stream_event text and thinking deltas through the existing estimated-token counter. All 361 provider tests and 361 race tests passed. All 15 cases across nine complete related browser files passed with zero retries in e2e-aEViEB, including held text/reasoning streams, held child counts with no parent leakage, parent identity, interruption, errors and complete results after reload. Native tool progress remains a replacement text window without an authoritative byte total; LeapMux preserves the window and does not invent a byte counter. Installed-source and local mock probes verified root and child fragments. All four generation-progress cases and the child live-transcript case passed in e2e-kJQmyK with zero retries. github-copilot.detailNote:
Copilot loads the MCP servers of a project (.mcp.json) only from a folder in its trusted list, which it shares with the Copilot CLI, but in server mode it asks nothing and leaves the question to its host. LeapMux asks instead: when a session opens in a folder that Copilot does not trust (session.permissions.folderTrust.isTrusted), the chat shows one question that names the folder. Trust adds the folder to Copilot's list (addTrusted) and loads the project's MCP servers in the running session (session.mcp.reload), with the repository hooks that Copilot deferred (sessions.loadDeferredRepoHooks). Do not trust keeps the servers unloaded, and the agent asks no more during its life. Instructions, custom agents and skills load either way, as in Copilot's own policy. The question is LeapMux's shared workspace-trust question, which other agents of the same kind can use.

Verified with Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through a private native probe of the trust store, the MCP discovery and the reload. All 83 Copilot browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-9H4UMA, including a project .mcp.json server in an untrusted folder that loaded after Trust, with the folder in Copilot's trusted list, and stayed unloaded after Do not trust, with no question after reload in either case. zcode.detailNote:
ZCode 3.16.3 runs a project's hooks (`hooks` in `.zcode/config.json`) only after the user trusts each one. When the first turn of a session starts, ZCode states the hooks that wait for trust in a `hookAdmission` update, and the turn runs without them. ZCode's own hook review reaches only a subscriber of its desktop protocol, so the stdio app-server asks LeapMux nothing. LeapMux asks the shared workspace-trust question when that turn ends. Trust subscribes to the session's conversation (`v4/conversation/subscribe`), asks ZCode for the review (`requestWorkspaceHookReview`), and trusts each hook that waits for trust (`respondWorkspaceHookReview`). ZCode keeps the grant for each hook, and the running session runs the hooks from its next prompt. Do not trust sends nothing, so the hooks stay blocked. Instruction files such as `AGENTS.md` load without trust.

Verified with ZCode 3.16.3 through a private native probe of a project hook: the review reached only a subscriber, and the answer let the hook run at the next prompt of the same session. All 93 ZCode browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-E90HHm, including a project hook that stayed blocked at the first prompt, then ran at the next prompt after Trust, and stayed blocked after Do not trust. The Kimi Code and GitHub Copilot cases of the shared question passed in the same run. All 2,878 tests of the ZCode, Kimi Code and GitHub Copilot packages and the shared provider kit passed under the race detector.

qoder-cli.detailNote:
LeapMux adds an Extended Thinking axis (Auto, Off, On) beside the effort. Off launches Qoder with --thinking disabled and the effort none, because Qoder turns thinking back on for any other explicit effort; the chosen effort stays in the settings. On launches with --thinking adaptive and the chosen effort. Auto sends no thinking flag. The effort menu no longer offers none, which Off replaces. A change restarts the agent with --resume. Qoder then restores the stored reasoning settings of the session unless the launch states an effort, so every launch states --reasoning-effort, with Qoder's own auto for Auto. This also corrects a return from a concrete effort to Auto, which kept the old effort before.

Verified with Qoder CLI 1.1.78 through private native probes of each launch and of a resumed session. The next model request proves each state (enable_thinking and reasoning_effort). All 88 Qoder browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-pmV0Nf, including Auto, Off, reload and On, Off across an effort change and a model switch, and the return to the automatic effort. codewhale.detailNote:
Verified with Codewhale 0.10.1 (fead51eeea0f). LeapMux exposes Auto, Normal and Concise. Auto preserves native configuration; explicit choices set CODEWHALE_VERBOSITY only for this agent process. The native thread and turn APIs have no verbosity field, so a change uses the existing process restart and resumes the same native thread. No shared configuration or prompt template is changed.

Native source and an isolated Normal -> Concise -> Normal probe confirm that only Concise adds Codewhale's own Concise Output Discipline instructions, while the thread, model and earlier conversation remain intact. All 614 provider tests and 614 race tests passed. All ten cases across complete output-style, model, reasoning-effort, session-resume and steer-mid-turn browser files passed with zero retries in e2e-7kygXG. The style proof also restores the inherited concise default through Auto, preserves prior user text across restarts, and retains style after a model switch and reload.

qwen-code.detailNote: Qwen Code 0.26.0 offers no request that changes a running session's output style: `session/set_config_option` handles mode, model and reasoning_effort alone, and the /output-style command works in the interactive UI only. The launch flag `--output-style <name>` applies in ACP mode: each of the four built-in styles (Concise, Proactive, Explanatory, Learning) appends its `# Output Style: <name>` section to the model system prompt, and an unknown name falls back to the default style with a warning (live probes .tmp/qwen-style-probe/drive-*.log). The Worker states the flag at launch (`qwenOutputStyleArgs`), serves the Output Style group (Auto + the four styles) as a local option group, and applies a change through a restart. Native acceptance: the output-style case passed in its first run (17.8s, e2e run of .tmp/qwen-style-probe/e2e.log); all 80 Qwen Code browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-bQJjBL; 177 package tests including the three new output-style tests.

codebuddy-code.detailNote:
CodeBuddy Code 2.173.0 reports output_style and available_output_styles through initialize. LeapMux exposes the native choices, preserves a configured custom style missing from the initial snapshot, and refreshes the catalog after turns. Catalog enrichment preserves the selected ID and does not assert that the process is active. Native name matching uses full Unicode lowercase conversion.

CodeBuddy retains the session's initial style, so set_config can acknowledge a change without applying it. LeapMux changes styles through a session-preserving process restart with a native --settings outputStyle override. Actual model requests prove Default, Concise, Explanatory and custom style instructions, while the profile's configured outputStyle remains unchanged.

All 81 CodeBuddy browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-2VHIC5 on 2026-10-24, including all three output-style scenarios. They cover conversation and session preservation, reloads, model switches, delayed custom-style discovery and profile preservation. All 444 package/race tests and full repository tests, lint and site validation passed. Source evidence comes from the installed 2.173.0 binary and isolated native protocol probes.

qoder-cli.detailNote:
LeapMux adds an Output Style axis for Qoder CLI. It lists Auto and the styles that Qoder's initialize reply states (default, Explanatory, Learning and the user's own styles), and shows the style that the session runs. A choice launches Qoder with --output-style; Auto sends no flag, so the style of Qoder's own settings applies. A change restarts the agent with --resume, because Qoder stores no style in the session and ignores a live flag-settings change.

Verified with Qoder CLI 1.1.78 through private native probes of new and resumed launches, a user style, an unknown name and the live request. The next model request's system prompt carries the selected style. All 88 Qoder browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-QGyQkz, including Auto, Explanatory before and after reload, Learning, a user style, Default and the return to Auto. All 396 Qoder backend tests and 396 race tests passed.

factory-droid.detailNote: Droid 0.249.0 has output styles (the built-in Default and Concise, plus custom styles), but only its own interactive UI can select one: the selector writes a per-session snapshot (setOutputStyleSessionSnapshot) that no protocol request reaches. The stream-jsonrpc session protocol that `droid exec` exposes states no output-style axis: droid.update_session_settings takes modelId, reasoningEffort, autonomyMode, interactionMode, autonomyLevel, specModeModelId, specModeReasoningEffort, missionSettings, tags and compaction fields alone, and the resolved settings of droid.initialize_session hold no outputStyle key. Live probes against the E2E mock (.tmp/droid-style-probe/drive-*.log) placed outputStyle at the root, under sessionDefaultSettings, under general.sessionDefaultSettings, in the user settings file, and with the invalid value no-such-style: no request gained the `# Output style: Concise` section, and the invalid value raised no diagnostic. The 0.233.0-era settings-file route that the earlier note described no longer exists.

amp.detailNote:
A native large-shell tool result retains its output inline. The result carries no native output pointer. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the native shell result of Amp keeps a 50,000-character tail with a `truncation.prefixLinesOmitted` count and carries no output pointer. The E2E spec proves the exact tail and the absence of a path row (native probes of the Amp tail limit recorded in the feature plan, spec checked 2026-10-05).

Tested version: Amp 0.0.1791074829.

claude-code.userNote: Claude Code reports the path of the file that holds the full output of a long tool result. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
claude-code.detailNote: user.tool_use_result.persistedOutputPath, or one exact persisted-output tool_result wrapper with Full output saved to. The extraction matches the pointer to its session_id and tool_use_id. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

cline.userNote: Cline keeps the start and the end of a long command output inline and cuts the middle. It reports no file that holds the full output, so LeapMux shows no output path.
cline.detailNote:
tool.finished.payload result retains the native run_commands head/tail. No filesystem output pointer exists on this selected native route. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: `truncateCommandOutput` of Cline 3.0.68 keeps 48,000 characters (head and tail) and inserts a notice that tells the model to refine the command; it writes no output file and states no path (source checked 2026-10-05).

codebuddy-code.userNote: CodeBuddy Code saves long tool output to a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
codebuddy-code.detailNote: user.message.content tool_result text contains the exact persisted-output wrapper and Full output saved to filesystem path. The extraction matches the wrapper to its session_id and tool_use_id. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

codewhale.userNote: When CodeWhale reports a file that holds a saved tool output, LeapMux shows its path before the original preview. LeapMux never reads that file.
codewhale.detailNote: item.completed.payload.item.metadata.spillover_path with tool_use_id and native descriptor scope. Bash detail also ends with the native Full output footer. artifact_id alone is insufficient. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

codex.userNote: Codex keeps command output in its result and saves no file for it, so LeapMux shows no output path. Upstream tracks [a request to save the full output](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49907).
codex.detailNote:
Native commandExecution retains aggregated output and omission counts. Its command/session IDs and command input paths are not output files. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the Codex 0.160.0 commandExecution item has aggregatedOutput, processId, exitCode and durationMs, and no output file path. Only image generation reports a saved path. Upstream issue 49907 asks Codex to save the full output of a truncated exec cell to a file, and it is open (checked 2026-10-05).

Sources fetched on 2026-10-05:
- <https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49907> (open): Asks Codex to save the full output of a truncated exec cell to a file and tell the model the path. The dropped middle is gone today.

command-code.userNote: Command Code reports the path of a saved full tool output. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
command-code.detailNote: tool_completed.event.result text contains the exact full output saved to footer, followed by native read_file guidance. The extraction matches the footer to its toolCallId and the shell_command tool. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

github-copilot.userNote: Copilot reports the path of the file that holds the output of a shell command. LeapMux shows the path and does not read the file.
github-copilot.detailNote:
tool.execution_complete result.contents shell_exit.outputFilePath is an explicit native filesystem path. The extraction matches the path to its parent session and toolCallId. One shellId can serve more than one call, so the toolCallId, not the shellId, identifies the row. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

The native tool.execution_complete event holds shell_exit.outputFilePath. One shell ID can serve more than one call, so LeapMux matches a path by the tool call ID.

cursor.userNote: Cursor sends only the exit code and the output text of a shell command. It sends no path for saved output, so LeapMux shows the output text only.
cursor.detailNote:
The selected native shell reply contains complete inline output and no fullOutputPath. Native process/blob IDs are not filesystem paths. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the Cursor 2026.09.28-64d2043 ACP agent forwards only exitCode, stdout, and stderr for a shell call and drops the native output_location field (installed bundle read 2026-10-05). The E2E mock never sets the native spill threshold, so the spec proves only the inline case. The local Cursor store may hold more than ACP sends.

deepseek-harness.userNote: DeepSeek Harness reports the path of saved output when a tool output spills to a file. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
deepseek-harness.detailNote: Native bash stream and dropped-output notices expose stdout and stderr spill paths. The spill-policy, grep and glob notices expose local stored-result locators. A native (unavailable) or could not be saved notice supplies no path, and the extraction rejects URI locators and opaque IDs. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

dirac.userNote: When a Dirac command prints very long output, Dirac saves the full output to a file and states its path. LeapMux shows the path and the original preview. LeapMux does not read the file.
dirac.detailNote: ACP rawOutput.output ends with exactly one Full output saved to filesystem path under `dirac/large-output-<native id>.log`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

factory-droid.userNote: Factory Droid saves the full output of a shell command to a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path with the result and keeps the original preview.
factory-droid.detailNote: Execute tool_result supplies a path under droid-terminal-*/<native UUID>.log. Droid 0.240.0 includes the whole-output path in its middle-cut notice. The parser also reads the native saved-output footer. LeapMux requires one valid absolute output path, retains the original inline preview, and reads no output file. The complete E2E spec compares the actual native file bytes and browser preview before and after reload. Complete-file acceptance: e2e-naTHwF.

fast-agent.detailNote:
Fast Agent 0.10.47 retains native bash and process results in its root-session history. Native Commands defaults to Off, which keeps the ACP host terminal. Enabling Native Commands withholds that capability and selects Fast Agent's local shell, which saves long output and states its filesystem path. Native Commands requires Bypass Permissions because the local shell does not request ACP approval. Changing either launch setting restarts the process and stops an active turn. LeapMux recovers root tool records at turn end with their original native arguments, results, timestamps and call IDs. It uses separate archive identities because live ACP calls use unrelated UUIDs. It preserves the native preview and structured exit status, displays the stated output paths before the preview, and keeps Copy on that preview. The adapter reads native history metadata; it does not read retained output files. The native provider owns file retention. Native probes: .tmp/fastagent-output-probe/drive-bash.log and drive-permissions-allow.log; root histories in run-hsFd4z and run-hUsm39. Cancellation evidence: interrupt.log and interrupt-kfndtB. Native acceptance (2026-10-26): e2e-PCcPKM passed all 81 Fast Agent browser cases with zero retries. The positive output-path file covers native exit 0, exit 7 and interruption, original retained-file bytes, preview preservation, Copy, reload and the next turn. The complete Fast Agent package passed 113 tests under the race detector, and 735 affected Vitest cases passed. Frontend typecheck and lint and backend lint passed. Evidence: .tmp/fastagent-directory-acceptance-3.log. The matrix assertion failed before promotion in .tmp/fastagent-matrix-before.log and passed afterward in .tmp/fastagent-matrix-after.log.

Track the native route and its LeapMux integration: https://github.com/leapmux/leapmux/issues/527.

gemini-cli.userNote: Gemini CLI can save large old tool output to a file and give its model the path. It does not send that path to LeapMux.
gemini-cli.detailNote:
Native tool-output masking exposes a filesystem path in subsequent model context. The selected ACP tool result and stored native record do not expose that pointer to this transcript hook. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit with medium confidence. Gemini CLI 0.62.0 replaces a large tool output in its model history with a tool_output_masked block that states the saved file path (upstream source checked 2026-10-05). The ACP tool result and the stored session record that LeapMux reads do not carry that block.

goose.detailNote: Goose 1.56.0 saves truncated native shell output and states each saved path. The Native Commands setting chooses the agent runtime instead of the ACP host terminal and applies through a restart; the default keeps the LeapMux terminal. The Goose plugin reads only complete native shell truncation notices and preserves the original tail preview. Native mock capture: .tmp/goose-native-output-capture.json (e2e-54noCX); browser acceptance of both default-terminal and native-command cases: e2e-hxgtjU, zero retries, with original file contents, Copy and reload proofs. Native acceptance: all 74 Goose browser cases passed with zero retries in e2e-AHUK0W; .tmp/goose-directory-acceptance.log EXIT 0 (Goose and Claude race tests, matrix scripts, and full Goose directory)

grok-build.userNote: Grok Build reports the path of the log file that holds the output of a shell command. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
grok-build.detailNote: ACP rawOutput type Bash carries output_file as an explicit native path. The extraction accepts the path only for its own call and native session under `sessions/<session>/terminal/<call>.log`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

junie.userNote: Junie reports the path of saved shell output in its session event log, not in the live tool update. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
junie.detailNote: Native SessionA2uxEvent TerminalBlockUpdatedEvent carries outputFile.relativePath. New execute ACP frame exposes no direct path. The extraction reads a pointer-only supplement for the exact native call and opens no output file. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

kilo.userNote: Kilo saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview. It does not read the file, and Kilo controls how long the file stays.
kilo.detailNote: Native OpenCode-family ACP rawOutput.metadata.outputPath is a filesystem path. The Kilo plugin reads the path through its own hook, which shares the OpenCode-family extraction. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

kimi-code.userNote: When Kimi Code saves a long tool output to a file, it states the path in the tool result. LeapMux shows that path before the original preview and never reads the file.
kimi-code.detailNote: tool_result.output includes native output_path in either the exact complete-output header or per-line footer. The extraction binds the path to its call, agent, session, and the native path format. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

kiro.userNote: Kiro reports the path of a saved tool output file. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
kiro.detailNote: ACP _meta.kiro.outputTransformation kind offloaded carries absFilePath. This is a native filesystem path, not a tool ID. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

letta-code.userNote: Letta Code ends a long tool result with the path of a file that holds the full output. LeapMux shows the path with the result and keeps the original preview.
letta-code.detailNote: Canonical tool_return_message tool_return ends with Full output written to filesystem path. The extraction rejects progress and lifecycle frames and keeps every real late final return. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

mimo-code.userNote: MiMo Code saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview and does not read the file.
mimo-code.detailNote: Native HTTP message.part.updated properties.part.state.metadata.outputPath is a filesystem path. The extraction matches the path to its part callID and sessionID. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

oh-my-pi.userNote: Oh My Pi identifies saved tool output with an artifact ID, not a file path, so LeapMux shows no output path.
oh-my-pi.detailNote:
Native result.details.meta.truncation.artifactId is a numeric ID, not a path. The artifact directory can be adopted; nonpersistent sessions keep in-memory artifacts. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

Classified as an agent limit: the native truncation metadata of Oh My Pi 18.6.0 holds artifactId, a numeric ID that the wire carries as a string, and artifact:// is a URI scheme. The artifact file name holds that ID and the tool type, and Oh My Pi reports no path for it. An opaque ID or URI does not supply a filesystem path.

opencode.userNote: OpenCode saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview. It does not read the file, and OpenCode controls how long the file stays.
opencode.detailNote: Native ACP rawOutput.metadata.outputPath is a filesystem path under `tool-output/tool_<native id>`. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

pi.userNote: Pi reports the path of the file that holds the full output of a long tool result. LeapMux shows the path before the preview and does not read the file.
pi.detailNote:
Native tool_execution_end.result.details.fullOutputPath is an explicit filesystem path. MCP and codemode retain their own native inline content. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

The Pi native result carries details.fullOutputPath (rpc-commands.md documents fullOutputPath for a truncated bash output).

qoder-cli.userNote: Qoder reports the path of a file that holds a saved tool output. LeapMux shows the path with the result and keeps the original preview.
qoder-cli.detailNote: Native user.tool_use_result.persistedOutput.path is a filesystem path. The extraction matches the path to its session_id and the exact tool_result.tool_use_id. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

reasonix.userNote: Large tool results show a link to the native saved output. The result row keeps Reasonix's preview.
reasonix.detailNote:
Re-evaluated on 2026-10-29 against the installed Reasonix v2.53.1 binary and matching source tag, revision 74805c102cf483aed637f30c9316928d3048c18c. Source: internal/runtime/agent/tool_output_spill.go. Large native results spill beside the session and report a Full output path plus opening lines. LeapMux validates the native receipt and call-specific filename, exposes the path before the unchanged preview, and preserves exact Copy after reload. The spec verifies the native file bytes and omitted middle/end markers.

Browser acceptance: all 1 case(s) in the complete spec passed with zero retries in e2e-sjioUn. The complete Reasonix run passed 84 cases in all 54 files.

zcode.userNote: ZCode saves long tool output in a file and reports its path. LeapMux shows the path above the preview and does not read the file.
zcode.detailNote: Native stored tool state.metadata.serialization.artifactPath is an explicit filesystem path. zcode-artifact URI alone is not a path. The extraction matches the path to its native session and call and the sanitized path segments. LeapMux keeps the original preview and reads no output file.

qwen-code.userNote: Qwen Code reports the path of saved shell output. LeapMux shows that path before the output preview and does not open the file.
qwen-code.detailNote: Native shell_result outputFiles supplies reported output file paths. Background shell results can report a native truncation footer. LeapMux checks the exact native call and its observed opener. It keeps the original preview and reads no native archive or output file.
